authority: State Agriculture Department / Seed Certification Agency

description.en: A Seed Dealer License is required by any person or entity engaged in the business of selling, offering for sale, bartering, or otherwise supplying seed of any notified kind or variety. The license is issued under the Seeds Act 1966 and is mandatory for operating as a seed dealer across India. It ensures that seeds sold to farmers meet quality standards and are traceable to certified sources.

verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must possess a prescribed educational qualification, typically a degree or diploma in Agriculture, Horticulture, or a related field. In some states, practical experience in the seed trade may substitute for formal qualifications.
The applicant must have adequate storage facilities that protect seeds from moisture, pests, and contamination, with proper labelling and record-keeping arrangements.

unverifiedEligibility: Specific educational qualifications vary by state — some accept B.Sc Agriculture, some accept diploma holders.
Some states require a minimum storage area (e.g., 100 sq ft) with specific ventilation and pest control measures.
Existing dealers may need to comply with updated infrastructure norms at renewal.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form for seed dealer license, available at the district agriculture office or state agriculture department portal.
Copies of educational qualification certificates — degree or diploma in Agriculture, Horticulture, or related field from a recognised university or institution.
Proof of premises for seed storage and sale — ownership documents, lease agreement, or rent receipt for the premises along with a layout plan showing storage area.
Identity proof such as Aadhaar card, PAN card, or voter ID of the applicant.
Recent passport-size photographs of the applicant.
Details of seed sources — names and addresses of seed producers, companies, or agencies from which seeds will be procured for sale.

processInformation.claim: Submit the prescribed application form along with required documents to the District Agriculture Officer or through the state agriculture department's online portal where available.
A Seed Inspector appointed under the Seeds Act visits the applicant's premises to verify the storage facilities, infrastructure, and compliance with prescribed norms.

Upon satisfactory inspection, the licensing authority (District Agriculture Officer or designated officer) grants the seed dealer license. The license is valid for a period of three years (may vary by state) and must be renewed before expiry.

output.claim: A Seed Dealer License is issued containing the dealer's name, address of premises, categories and varieties of seeds authorised for sale, validity period, and conditions of license. The dealer must display the license at the place of business.

fees.applicability: Seed dealer license application and issuance fee
fees.claim: License fee ranges from Rs. 500 to Rs. 2,000 depending on the state. Renewal fees are generally the same or slightly lower. Some states charge additional fees for inspection.

processingTime.applicability: Seed dealer license from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: Processing typically takes 30-60 days including the time for premises inspection and document verification. Delays may occur if the premises do not meet prescribed norms on initial inspection.

sources.title: Seeds Act 1966 and Seed Rules — via Seednet India Portal
sources.publisher: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Seeds Act 1966 regulates the quality of seeds sold in India. Section 7 requires any person carrying on the business of selling seeds of any notified kind or variety to obtain a license from the prescribed authority. The Seed Rules prescribe the qualifications for dealers and conditions of licensing.
claimsSupported: Seed dealer license is mandatory under Seeds Act 1966.
Educational qualification and storage infrastructure are licensing conditions.
License is valid for three years and renewable.
sources.uncertainty: State-level rules may prescribe additional or different qualifications and conditions.

sources.title: Seednet India Portal — Seed Dealer Information
sources.publisher: National Informatics Centre / Department of Agriculture
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Seednet portal provides information on seed dealer licensing requirements, state-wise contact details for licensing authorities, and links to state agriculture department portals for online applications.
claimsSupported: Fee ranges from Rs. 500 to Rs. 2,000 depending on the state.
Documents include identity proof, qualification proof, premises proof, and seed source details.
sources.uncertainty: Fee and processing time are indicative and vary by state.

limitations: This record provides a general overview based on central legislation. State-specific rules, fees, and qualification requirements may differ significantly.
Some states have moved to online licensing; others still require physical submission.
The record does not cover wholesale seed dealer licenses or seed producer licenses which have separate requirements.
License conditions such as record-keeping obligations and return filing are not detailed.
The Seeds Bill to replace the Seeds Act 1966, if enacted, may change licensing requirements.
